title: SQL Day 5 — CASE WHEN & Business Classification
description: Convert raw values into business categories and conditional metrics with CASE WHEN.

topics.title: CASE WHEN Fundamentals
topics.business_skill: Create business classifications from row-level rules.

teaching.teacher: ## CASE WHEN\nCASE evaluates conditions and returns a chosen result for the first matching WHEN.
teaching.explain: It turns raw numeric or text values into labels used by business teams.
teaching.detailedlearning: Order conditions from most specific to least specific and include ELSE when an unmatched value needs a defined category.
teaching.expose: CASE is business-rule encoding, so validate the rules and boundaries before coding.
teaching.example: CASE WHEN sales >= 1500 THEN 'High' WHEN sales >= 500 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'Low' END AS sales_band
teaching.business_question: The manager wants orders classified as High, Medium, or Low value.
teaching.expected_sql: SELECT order_id, sales, CASE WHEN sales >= 1500 THEN 'High' WHEN sales >= 500 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'Low' END AS sales_band FROM orders;

questions.request: Classify each order as High when sales are at least 1500, Medium when sales are at least 500, otherwise Low.
Classify rows as Loss for profit below zero and Profit for zero or above.

questions.scenario: Operations needs a shipment priority label.
questions.request: Classify orders as Premium for First Class, Standard for Second Class, and Economy otherwise.

teaching.teacher: ## Compound CASE\nEach WHEN can contain AND/OR logic, allowing multi-factor classifications.
teaching.explain: CASE can evaluate several columns together to create a business segment.
teaching.detailedlearning: Use parentheses for OR branches and test boundary cases deliberately.
teaching.expose: Complex CASE statements should be written from business rules, not improvised while typing.
teaching.example: CASE WHEN sales >= 1000 AND profit > 0 THEN 'High Value Profitable' WHEN sales >= 1000 THEN 'High Value Loss' ELSE 'Other' END
teaching.business_question: Commercial leadership wants high-value orders split by profitability.
teaching.expected_sql: SELECT order_id, sales, profit, CASE WHEN sales >= 1000 AND profit > 0 THEN 'High Value Profitable' WHEN sales >= 1000 THEN 'High Value Loss' ELSE 'Other' END AS segment FROM orders;

questions.scenario: High-value orders must be separated by profit status.
questions.request: Classify orders as High Value Profitable, High Value Loss, or Other.

questions.scenario: Leadership wants West Technology orders identified separately.
questions.request: Create a label for rows that are both West and Technology, with Other for all remaining rows.

questions.scenario: Finance defines healthy transactions as sales at least 1000 and profit margin proxy profit/sales at least 10%.
questions.request: Create Healthy, High Sales Low Margin, and Other labels using sales and profit.

topics.title: Conditional Aggregation
topics.business_skill: Calculate KPI subsets inside one grouped query.

teaching.teacher: ## Conditional aggregation\nSUM(CASE WHEN ... THEN ... ELSE ... END) and COUNT(CASE WHEN ... THEN 1 END) let one query calculate multiple conditional KPIs.
teaching.explain: Instead of filtering the entire dataset, conditionally include rows in individual measures.
teaching.detailedlearning: This is powerful for dashboards because several business segments can be compared in one row.
teaching.expose: The condition belongs inside the aggregate when you need multiple subsets side by side.
teaching.example: SUM(CASE WHEN profit < 0 THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS loss_sales
teaching.business_question: The CFO wants profitable and loss-making sales side by side.
teaching.expected_sql: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN profit >= 0 THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS profitable_sales, SUM(CASE WHEN profit < 0 THEN sales ELSE 0 END) AS loss_sales FROM orders;

questions.scenario: Finance needs profitable sales and loss sales.
questions.request: Return profitable sales and loss-making sales as separate metrics.

questions.scenario: The manager wants order counts by value band in one result.
questions.request: Return counts for High, Medium, and Low sales bands.

questions.scenario: The region review needs total sales and loss sales for each region.
questions.request: Return region, total sales, loss sales, and profitable sales.
questions.validation: GROUP BY region with conditional aggregates

teaching.teacher: ## Business ordering\nCASE can create a custom sort priority when alphabetical or numeric ordering is not appropriate.
teaching.explain: Create a ranking expression that maps business priority to a number.
teaching.detailedlearning: Use CASE in ORDER BY when stakeholders specify an explicit sequence.
teaching.expose: Display labels and sort logic can be different fields.
teaching.example: ORDER BY CASE WHEN category='Technology' THEN 1 WHEN category='Furniture' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END
teaching.business_question: Management wants Technology first, Furniture second, and all other categories afterward.
teaching.expected_sql: SELECT category, SUM(sales) AS sales FROM orders GROUP BY category ORDER BY CASE WHEN category='Technology' THEN 1 WHEN category='Furniture' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END;

questions.scenario: Technology must appear first in the management report.
questions.request: Sort category results with Technology first, Furniture second, and remaining categories after them.

questions.scenario: Loss-making regions should be reviewed before profitable regions.
questions.request: Sort regions so negative-profit regions appear first.

questions.scenario: A review queue prioritizes High Value Loss, High Value Profitable, then Other.
questions.request: Sort order-level classifications in that business priority.

topics.title: CASE-Driven Management KPI
topics.business_skill: Build a business-ready classification and KPI query.

teaching.teacher: ## KPI classification\nCombine classification with aggregation to turn raw transactions into management segments.
teaching.explain: The classification must be consistent at row level before aggregating it.
teaching.detailedlearning: A robust pattern is: classify rows in a subquery/CTE, then aggregate the classified result.
teaching.expose: Separating classification from aggregation improves readability and validation.
teaching.example: WITH classified AS (SELECT *, CASE WHEN sales>=1500 THEN 'High' ELSE 'Standard' END AS band FROM orders) SELECT band, COUNT(*) AS orders, SUM(sales) AS sales FROM classified GROUP BY band;
teaching.business_question: The sales director wants order volume and sales by value band.
teaching.expected_sql: WITH classified AS (SELECT *, CASE WHEN sales>=1500 THEN 'High' ELSE 'Standard' END AS band FROM orders) SELECT band, COUNT(*) AS orders, SUM(sales) AS sales FROM classified GROUP BY band;

questions.scenario: Management wants sales by order-value band.
questions.request: Return band, order count, and total sales for High versus Standard orders using the stated threshold.

questions.scenario: Finance wants profit performance by profit status.
questions.request: Return profit status, order count, sales, and profit.

questions.scenario: The executive dashboard needs regional value-band performance.
questions.request: Return region, value band, order count, sales, and profit.
